rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Al-Hashr can mean resurrection or gathering; the first sense is intended here.
rows.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" : الحشر يجيىء بمعنى البعث والجمع والأول هو المراد هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person is literally deprived of sight at the Resurrection, as in the verse about being gathered blind, mute, and deaf.
rows.anchor: فاقد البصر كما في قوله تعالى :

rows.speaker: عرائس البقلى
rows.claim: The inward blindness is ignorance of the Real's existence in this life, continuing into the next.
rows.anchor: وفي "عرائس البقلى" : يعني جاهلا بوجود الحق كما كان جاهلا في الدنيا

rows.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Ali says that whoever does not know God in this world will not know Him in the next.
rows.anchor: كما قال علي رضي الله عنه : من لم يعرف الله في الدنيا لا يعرفه في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The introductory قال resumes the preceding account as an explanatory answer; Rabb is addressed as Lord.
rows.anchor: استئناف بياني {رب} (اى روردكارمن)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question contrasts the person's blindness at resurrection with his sight in worldly life.
rows.anchor: أي : في الدنيا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revealed verses, proofs of divine power, and signs of oneness were clear and apparent to everyone.
rows.anchor: آيات الكتاب أو دلائل القدرة وعلامات الوحدة واضحة نيرة بحيث لا تخفى على أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting means becoming blind to the signs and abandoning them like something utterly forgotten.
rows.anchor: أي : عميت عنها وتركتها ترك المنسي الذي لا يذكر أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As he neglected the signs in life, he is left blind in punishment as fitting recompense; the blindness, muteness, and deafness are eventually removed so he sees the terrors and his place in Hell.
rows.anchor: تترك في العمى والعذاب جزاء وفاقا لكن لا أبدا كما قيل بل إلى ما شاء الله ثم يزيله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives a recompense corresponding to the offense.
rows.anchor: {وكذالك} أي : ومثل ذلك الجزاء الموافق للجناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israf is exceeding the limit in any human action, though the term is most familiar in connection with spending.
rows.anchor: والإسراف مجاوزة الحد في كل فعل يفعله الإنسان وإن كان ذلك في الإنفاق أشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are the Qur'an and the other miracles, which the offender denied and turned away from.
rows.anchor: أي : بالقرآن وسائر المعجزات بل كذبها وأعرض عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may refer to punishment in the Hereafter generally or specifically to the punishment of the Fire.
rows.anchor: على الإطلاق أو عذاب النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife punishment is more severe than worldly punishment such as constricted livelihood.
rows.anchor: مما نعذبهم به في الدنيا من ضنك العيش ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment lasts longer and does not end.
rows.anchor: وأدوم لعدم انقطاعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To escape punishment and gain reward, one should endure worldly hardships in obedience and avoid sins and worldly desires; Paradise is surrounded by hardships and Hell by desires.
rows.anchor: فعليه أن يصبر على شدائد الدنيا في طاعة الله ويجتنب المعاصي وشهوات الدنيا فإن الجنة قد حفت بالمكاره وحفت النار بالشهوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a report, God sends Gabriel to inspect Paradise and then Hell; after each is surrounded respectively by hardships and desires, Gabriel fears few will enter Paradise and few will avoid Hell.
rows.anchor: دعا الله جبريل فأرسله إلى الجنة فقال : انظر إليها وإلى ما أعددت لأهلها فيها فرجع فقال : وعزتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A narration describes the people of Hell shackled and dragged face-down, struck by angels, and returned whenever they try to escape.
rows.anchor: روي أن أهل النار إذا انتهوا إلى أبوابها استقبلتهم الزبانية بالأغلال والسلاسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says the least punished person in Hell wears two sandals that make his brain boil.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "إن أدنى أهل النار عذابا الذي يجعل له نعلان يغلي منهما دماغه في رأسه"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sensible person should avoid the causes of punishment and blindness and strive not to be resurrected blind; separation from God, the Giver, is the most severe torment.
rows.anchor: وأشد العذاب عذاب القطيعة من الله الوهاب.

words: وَقَالُوا۟ لَوْلَا يَأْتِينَا بِـَٔايَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦٓ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers are the Quraysh disbelievers, demanding a sign of the kind they and their associates proposed, such as those given to Moses and Jesus.
rows.anchor: يعني كفار قريش : {لولا} هلا {يأتينا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their stubbornness reached the point that they refused to count the miracles they had already witnessed as signs.
rows.anchor: بلغوا من العناد إلى حيث لم يعدوا ما شاهدوا من المعجزات من قبيل الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza denies that the proof failed to arrive; the waw joins the question to an omitted preceding clause, and bayyina means a clear rational or sensory indication.
rows.anchor: الهمزة لإنكار الوقوع والواو للعطف على مقدر والبينة الدلالة الواضحة عقلية كانت أو حسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suhuf is the plural of sahifa, a written page; the author says the alphabet letters are separate pages among what was sent down to Adam.
rows.anchor: والصحف جمع صحيفة وهي التي يكتب فيها وحروف التهجي صحيفة على حدة مما أنزل على آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier pages refer to the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and the other revealed books.
rows.anchor: والمراد بها التوراة والإنجيل والزبور وسائر الكتب السماوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof is the Qur'an, which explains for people the true doctrines and foundational rulings shared by all messengers; it is the greatest sign of all.
rows.anchor: القرآن الذي فيه بيان للناس وما عبارة عن العقائد الحقية وأصول الأحكام التي اجتمعت عليها كافة الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an contains the essence of earlier revelation, verifies its truth and its accounts of past nations, and is itself an inimitable proof that can establish the truth of the other books.
rows.anchor: وهو شاهد بحقية ما فيها وبصحة ما ينطق به من أنباء الأمم من حيث أنه غني بإعجازه عما يشهد بحقيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its inclusion of the earlier books' core teachings, despite its bearer being unlettered and never studying them, makes its miraculous character clear.
rows.anchor: اشتماله على زبدة ما فيها مع أن الآتي به أمي لم يرها ولم يتعلم ممن علمها إعجاز بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic proof leaves no excuse for abandoning the revealed laws and following the path of error, a point the next verse develops.
rows.anchor: ثم بين أنه لا عذر لهم في ترك الشرائع وسلوك طريق الضلالة بوجه ما فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each of the two sides, the Prophet's party and the opponents, waits for the outcome of their affairs.
rows.anchor: انتظار الأمر أو زواله منتظرا لما يؤول إليه أمرنا وأمركم.

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi glosses this as the opponents waiting for the Prophet's misfortune while the believers await their punishment.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (يعني شما نكبت ما راشم ميداريد وما عقوبت شمارا).

rows.speaker: الكبير
rows.claim: Al-Kabir says each side awaits the outcome before death through jihad and the rise of power, or after death through reward and punishment, with honor for the truthful and humiliation for the false.
rows.anchor: قال في "الكبير" : كل منا ومنكم منتظر عاقبة أمره إما قبل الموت بسبب الجهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists said they would wait for time's events until Muhammad died and they were rid of him; God answers that they should wait.
rows.anchor: وروي أن المشركين قالوا : نتربص بمحمد حوادث الدهر فإذا مات تخلصنا فقال تعالى : {فتربصوا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God's command arrives soon, the parties will learn which of them follows the straight path.
rows.anchor: عن قريب إذا جاء أمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A straight path is a way without bends or deviation, following a balanced course.
rows.anchor: والصراط من السبيل ما لا التواء فيه أي : لا إعوجاج بل يكون على سبيل القصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks which side escaped misguidance: the Prophet's side or theirs.
rows.anchor: من الضلال أي : أنحن أم أنتم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A verse of poetry pictures the eventual exposure of the truth: when the dust clears, one will see whether a horseman or a donkey is beneath him.
rows.anchor: كما قال بعضهم : سوف ترى إذا انجلى الغبار أفرس تحتك أم حمار

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi identifies the Prophet as the one intended: he is both guided and a guide to others.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (مراد حضرت يغمبرست كه هم راه يافته وهم راه نماينده است)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, the guided reach God by traversing the spiritual stations and detaching from all besides Him; the others cut themselves off by attaching to something else.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى المهتدين بالوصول إليه بقطع المنازل والانفصال عما سواه والمنقطعين عنه باتصال غيره

rows.speaker: الخجندي
rows.claim: Khujandi's couplet says union is attained only by severance, beginning with separation from all else.
rows.anchor: كما قال الخجندي : وصل ميسر نشود جز بقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has removed excuses by granting respite and guidance; the decisive proof belongs to God.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الله تعالى قطع المعذرة بالإمهال و"الإرشاد" فلله الحجة البالغة

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: A Prophetic report names three who plead excuses before God: one who died in the interval, someone without reason, and a child; they are tested with a fire, and their response reveals their standing.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال : قال عليه السلام : "يحتج على الله ثلاثة

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf reports that the people of Paradise recite no Qur'an except Surat Ta Ha and Ya Sin.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "لا يقرأ أهل الجنة من القرآن إلا سورة طه ويس"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although rain issues from the lowest heaven, the plural heavens are mentioned because all have a role in producing rain, whose effects originate from above.
rows.anchor: جمع السموات لأن لها مدخلا في الأمطار إذ التأثير إنما يحصل من جهة العلو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening or separation is an eternal divine attribute; its relation to the created object occurs in time, as with other attributes, so al-Baydawi's calling it contingent is wrong.
rows.anchor: فقول البيضاوي إن الفتق عارض خطأ كما في "بحر العلوم"

words: وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ حَىٍّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water is a fluid body surrounding the earth; every animal's origin is from water, with the generic definite article pointing to the kind of water, semen.
rows.anchor: الماء جسم سيال قد أحاط حول الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean each animal individual comes from its particular father's semen, or each animal species from the semen proper to that species.
rows.anchor: أي : كل فرد من أفراد الدواب من نطفة معينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author distinguishes the living from animals: every animal is living, but not every living being is an animal, as with angels.
rows.anchor: قد فرقوا بين الحي والحيوان بأن كل حيوان حي وليس كل حي حيوانا كالملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some narrations say angels were created from wind made from water, Adam from soil, and jinn from fire.
rows.anchor: من "أن الله تعالى خلق الملائكة من ريح خلقها من الماء وآدم من تراب خلقه منه والجن من نار خلقها منه"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpreters include plants and trees because they grow through water; life can mean the vegetative faculty present in plants and animals.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : يدخل في الآية النبات والشجر لنمائهما بالماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes the polytheists for failing to believe despite these clear signs.
rows.anchor: آيا نمى كردند مشركان باوجود اين آيات واضحة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya interpretation reads the verse as indicating that the souls of believers and unbelievers were created before the heavens and earth; a report dates souls before bodies by two million years, with another version giving four thousand.
rows.anchor: في "التأويلات النجمية" يشير بقوله {أولم ير الذين كفروا أن السماوات والارض كانتا رتقا ففتقناهما}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says God created spirits before bodies by two million years; another version says four thousand years.
rows.anchor: خلق الأرواح قبل الأجساد بألفي ألف عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is called a roof because it is like a roof over the earth.
rows.anchor: سميت سقفا لأنها للأرض كالسقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is protected from falling despite having no pillars, from corruption until the appointed time, or from eavesdropping by devils through shooting stars.
rows.anchor: من الوقوع مع كونها بغير عمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gnostic's heart is a protected heaven, guarded from the whispers of human and jinn devils; a Prophetic prayer asks God to fill the heart with remembrance and drive away satanic whispers.
rows.anchor: أن سماء قلب العارف محفوظة من وساوس شيطان الإنس والجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites Masnavi verses saying God's remembrance burns away demonic whispers and diverts the narcissus eye from the vulture.
rows.anchor: ذكر حق كن بانك غولانرا بسوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavenly signs include sun, moon, stars, and other clear markers of God's existence, oneness, perfect workmanship, power, and wisdom; the heedless do not reflect and remain in error.
rows.anchor: أدلتها الواضحة التي خلقها الله تعالى فيها وجعلها علامات نيرة على وجوده ووحدته وكمال صنعه وعظيم قدرته وباهر حكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away from the signs means failing to contemplate them and persisting in unbelief and error.
rows.anchor: لا يتدبرون فيها فيقفون على ما هم عليه من الكفر والضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten traits of the abdals are purity of heart, generosity, truthful speech, humility, patience, private weeping, advising others, compassion for believers, reflection, and learning from things; one should contemplate creation to find knowledge of God.
rows.anchor: أخلاق الأبدال عشرة أشياء : سلامة في الصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David saw a tiny worm in his prayer niche and wondered whether God valued its creation; God made it speak, saying it remembered and thanked Him more than David did.
rows.anchor: روي أن داود عليه السلام دخل في محرابه فرأى دودة صغيرة فتفكر في خلقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True perception of signs means remembering God in everything, a mark of complete believers; spiritual blindness and turning away characterize ignorant unbelievers.
rows.anchor: فالمقصود برؤية الآيات بالحق ذكر الله تعالى عند كل شيء وهي من أوصاف المؤمنين الكاملين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites Masnavi lines portraying deniers as unable, like asses, to recognize the pearl-like value of divine knowledge.
rows.anchor: منكر بحرست وكوهر هاى او كى بود حيوان درو يرايه جو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is the earth's shadow, day the sun's light, the sun a luminous daytime star, and the moon a luminous nighttime star; God alone brought them from nonexistence into existence, showing perfect power and wisdom.
rows.anchor: الذي هو ظل الأرض {والنهار} الذي هو ضوء الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each refers to the sun and moon separately; in an orbit is its predicate, while swimming is a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: كل واحد من الشمس والقمر وهو مبتدأ خبره قوله : {فى فلك}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Swimming is swift motion through water or air; it is borrowed here for the stars' motion across their orbits.
rows.anchor: فإن السبح المر السريع في الماء أو في الهواء

rows.speaker: شرح التقويم
rows.claim: One view holds each celestial body fixed within its sphere like a signet set in a ring, immersed like a ball in water; spheres move by will and the stars move incidentally.
rows.anchor: قال في "شرح التقويم" : كل واحد من الكواكب مركوز في فلك

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another literal reading takes the sphere as a wave held back from flowing beneath the sky, in which sun and moon swim like fish; the sphere is a transparent body surrounding the world.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم أخذا بظاهر الآية : إن الفلك موج مكفوف من السيلان

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines falak as the course of the celestial bodies, named for its resemblance to a spindle whorl.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الفلك مجرى الكواكب وتسميته بذلك لكونه كالفلك

rows.speaker: محيى السنة
rows.claim: Muhyi al-Sunna says falak in Arabic means any round thing; its plural is aflak, as in a spindle whorl.
rows.anchor: وقال محيى السنة الفلك في كلام العرب كل شيء مستدير جمعه أفلاك ومنه فلكة المغزل

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh lays out three possible motions: a fixed sphere with moving stars, a moving sphere with stars also moving within it, or a moving sphere carrying stationary stars.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ : اختلف الناس في حركات الكواكب والوجوه الممكنة فيها ثلاثة

rows.speaker: الفلاسفة
rows.claim: The philosophers reject the first two motion models because they would rupture the spheres, and conclude that the spheres move while the stars are fixed in them.
rows.anchor: قال الفلاسفة : الرأي الأول باطل لأنه يوجب خرق الفلك وهو محال وكذا الرأي الثاني

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam rejects the philosophers' assumption that spheres cannot rupture: all three models are possible and within God's power; the Qur'an's apparent sense is fixed spheres with stars swimming inside them.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام : واعلم أن مدار هذا الكلام على امتناع الخرق على الأفلاك وهو باطل بل الحق أن الاحتمالات الثلاثة كلها ممكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without the sun and moon and their motions producing day, night, heat, cold, and other benefits, the blessings of the created heaven would not be complete.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه لو خلق السماء ولم يخلق الشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: ابن سينا
rows.claim: Ibn Sina argues that the celestial bodies are living and rational because the verse says they swim and Joseph's dream describes the stars prostrating; he says the rational plural is used only for rational beings.
rows.anchor: واحتج أبو علي بن سينا على كون الكواكب أحياء ناطقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rational plural does not prove that stars are rational: they are given rational pronouns because swimming and prostrating are actions associated with rational beings; the same usage occurs in the command to enter dwellings.
rows.anchor: والجواب أنه لما أسند إليهم ما هو من أفعال العقلاء وهو السباحة والسجود نزلن منزلة العقلاء

rows.speaker: بعض أهل الحقيقة
rows.claim: Some people of spiritual realization describe the celestial bodies' movers as immaterial, rational celestial souls, separate from bodily matter in essence but connected to the spheres in motion.
rows.anchor: قال بعض أهل الحقيقة : الأجرام الفلكية هي الأجسام فوق العناصر من الأفلاك والكواكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion answers an objection about rational speech as the human differentia: speech means what proceeds from the heart, not the tongue, and angels, jinn, and parrots have no such heart.
rows.anchor: والجواب الحق هو ما يجري على الجنان لا ما يجري على اللسان وليس لهم جنان حتى يجري عليه الشيء

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi reads night and day as the contraction and expansion of gnostics: at times majesty overwhelms them with contraction, at others beauty hosts them in expansion and generosity.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (در كشف الاسرار آورده كه نزد اهل اشارت شب وروز

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi takes the sun as the person of divine unity, settled through empowerment in the witnessing presence and neither increasing nor decreasing in certainty.
rows.anchor: آفتاب نشانه صاحب توحيداست بنعمت تمكين در حضرت شهود آراسته نه فزايد ونه كاهد

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi takes the moon as people of changing spiritual states, waxing and waning between the vanishing of unity's light and the full moon of the comprehensive station.
rows.anchor: وقمر نشانه اهل تلوين است كاه دركاهش بود وكاه در افزايش زمانى بظهور نور برق وحدت درمحاق نيستى افتد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words are framed as reported speech: they say that Abraham knows the idols are not capable of speaking, so why tell them to ask the idols.
rows.anchor: على إرادة القول أي : قائلين لقد علمت يا إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters admitted this because they were bewildered.
rows.anchor: فأقروا بهذا للحيرة التي لحقتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham rebukes them for knowingly worshipping something that can neither benefit them if worshipped nor harm them if neglected; such knowledge demands abandoning its worship.
rows.anchor: أتعلمون ذلك فتعبدون {من دون الله} أي : حال كونكم متجاوزين

words: أُفٍّۢ لَّكُمْ وَلِمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uff is an expression of vexation, meaning foulness and repulsiveness; grammarians also treat it as a verbal noun meaning I am vexed.
rows.anchor: وأف صوت التضجر إذا صوت بها الإنسان علم أنه متضجر ومعناه قبحا ونتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām identifies the objects of Abraham's vexation: the people and their idols; grammarians classify uff among verbal nouns.
rows.anchor: واللام لبيان المتأفف له أي : لكم ولآلهتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke asks whether they have lost their minds and failed to understand the ugliness of their conduct.
rows.anchor: {أفلا تعقلون} أي : أجننتم فلا تعقلون قبح صنيعكم

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata says God calls people to Himself and cuts them off from all else: why rely on an equally helpless creature instead of the One who controls harm, benefit, and the return.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء دعا الله تعالى عباده إليه وقطعهم عما دونه بقوله : {أفتعبدون}

words: مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمْ شَيْـًۭٔا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ
rows.speaker: حمدون القصار
rows.claim: Hamdun al-Qassar says that creatures seeking help from creatures is like one prisoner seeking help from another.
rows.anchor: قال حمدون القصار : استغاثة الخلق بالخلق كاستغاثة المسجون بالمسجون

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Some spiritual masters say seeking another reveals distance from God; all besides Him is play and falsehood, so detach from all else and rely on the Lord, who suffices for every need.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الكبار طلبك من غيره لوجود بعدك عنه إذ لو كنت حاضرا بقلبك معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Habib al-Ajami's wife urged him to earn wages; after he worshipped all night, he said he had worked for the Generous One and was ashamed to ask payment. Three days later she demanded wages or divorce; the next night he returned to find food and a bag of gold, sent by God, and she repented.
rows.anchor: حكي أن امرأة حبيب العجمي ألحت عليه أن يعمل بالأجرة طلبا للسعة في الرزق فخرج من بيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Affliction hastens punishment for idolaters and unbelievers, but for patient believers it raises their rank, erases sins, and transforms their base being; patience and gratitude are called for in both good and adversity.
rows.anchor: بل هو في حقهم تعجيل لعذابهم وفي حق المؤمنين الصابرين تكميل لدرجاتهم وحط من خطيآتهم وإكسير لنحاس وجودهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites Masnavi verses calling patience a rare alchemy and key to relief, urging gratitude for good and ill, and counseling patience because every blessing is paired with sorrow.
rows.anchor: صد هزاران كيميا حق آفريد كيميايى همو صبر آدم نديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Nun, the one associated with the fish, is the prophet Yunus ibn Matta; the author vocalizes Matta with an open mīm and doubled, open tāʾ.
rows.anchor: {وذا النون} أي : واذكر صاحب النون أي : الحوت والمراد يونس بن متى

rows.speaker: جامع الأصول
rows.claim: Jami al-Usul says Matta was the name of Yunus's mother.
rows.anchor: قيل : هو اسم أم يونس كذا في "جامع الأصول"

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Atā asked Kaʿb whether Matta was Yunus's father or mother; Kaʿb said it was his father's name and that his mother Badura descended from Aaron.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء : سألت كعبا عن متى أهو اسم أبيه أم أمه فقال : اسم أبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yunus was called Dhu al-Nun because the fish swallowed him.
rows.anchor: وسمي يونس بذي النون لأنه ابتلعه الحوت

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli says Dhu al-Nun is more honorific than companion of the fish in a passage praising Yunus; dhu makes the following noun principal, and nun is nobler than hut because it is an alphabet letter appearing at a surah's opening.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام السهيلي أضافه هنا إلى النون وقد قال في سورة القلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse commands recalling Yunus's departure in anger from the people of Nineveh near Mosul, after their long resistance to his preaching; he emigrated before being ordered to do so.
rows.anchor: أي : اذكر خبره وقت ذهابه حال كونه {مغاضبا} مراغما لقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form of the verb conveys the completeness and intensity of Yunus's anger.
rows.anchor: وبناء المفاعلة للدلالة على كمال غضبه والمبالغة فيه

rows.speaker: نجم الدين
rows.claim: An alternative account says Yunus warned his people of a fixed-time punishment and left; after they repented and punishment was averted, he thought they had made him a liar and departed angry. Najm al-Din's account is preferred by people of certainty.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول أنسب بتقرير الشيخ نجم الدين في "تأويلاته"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here naqdir means constrain, not be unable: Arabic uses the verb for restricting one's household, and Yunus's state is presented as though he thought God would not constrict him.
rows.anchor: لن نضيق عليه الأمر يقال قدر على عياله قدرا ضيق

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya reading says intense anger clouds judgment and veils faith's light, so one may think something unworthy of God, even if a prophet; Muhammad's strength was to speak only truth in anger and calm.
rows.anchor: في "التأويلات النجمية" يشير إلى أن الإنسان إذا استولى عليه الغضب يلتبس عليه عقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adds that God's grace toward sinful servants means He reproves prophets for wishing punishment on their people or disliking its removal, and wants them to seek forgiveness for them.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة أخرى وهي أن الله تعالى من كمال فضله وكرمه على عباده وإن كانوا عصاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Yunus boarded a ship that stopped at sea; the sailors drew lots three times and chose him each time, so he confessed, threw himself overboard, and was swallowed by a fish that God commanded not to harm him but to hold him as a prisoner.
rows.anchor: روي أنه حين خرج مغاضبا أتى بحر الروم فوجد قوما هيأوا السفينة فركب معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fā in fanādā is explanatory: the omitted events of the lots and the fish's swallowing occurred, then Yunus called out.
rows.anchor: الفاء فصيحة أي : فكان ما كان من القرعة والتقام الحوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The darknesses may be one overwhelming darkness or the combined darknesses of the fish's belly, the sea, and the night.
rows.anchor: في الظلمة الشديدة المتكافئة أو في ظلمات بطن الحوت والبحر والليل

rows.speaker: السمرقندي
rows.claim: Al-Samarqandi suggests the darknesses came from six directions, like a Prophetic report about a person surrounded by darkness in front, behind, on both sides, above, and below.
rows.anchor: وقال الشيخ السمرقندي في تفسيره وعندي والله أعلم أن تلك الظلمات كانت من الجهات الست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report describes a member of the community enclosed in six directions of darkness and bewildered.
rows.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام : "ورأيت رجلا من أمتي من بين يديه ظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An means that Yunus called out by declaring that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: أي : بأنه {لا إله إلا أنت}

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya reading likens the noble spirit cast into worldly life to Yunus swallowed by the whale of the commanding soul; by God's command the soul must not harm it, serving instead as its enclosure and prison.
rows.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" يشير إلى أن الروح الشريف إذا ألقي في بحر الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirit's rare safety from the soul's harm is like Yunus's safety in the fish; in the darkness of soul, body, and world, it calls on God alone to preserve it and inspire remembrance.
rows.anchor: ومن سلامة الروح أن يناديه في ظلمة النفس وظلمة القالب وظلمة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yunus declares God above incapacity and recognizes that his affliction did not occur without a cause on his own part.
rows.anchor: أنزهك تنزيها لائقا بك من أن يعجزك شيء وأن يكون ابتلائي هذا بغير سبب من جهتي

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya interpretation says Yunus declared God free of injustice toward him, even though God creates human acts.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : نزهه عن الظلم عليه وإن كان فعله بخلق فيه كما قال تعالى :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yunus ascribes wrongdoing to himself, acknowledging that he exposed himself to danger by hastily emigrating; this self-blame observes proper spiritual etiquette.
rows.anchor: ونسب الظلم إلى نفسه اعترافا واستحقاقا ورعاية للأدب فقال : {إني كنت من الظالمين}

rows.speaker: عرائس البقلى
rows.claim: Al-Baqli says God intended Yunus to have an ascent and witnessing in the fish's belly; there he saw, beneath the earth, what Muhammad saw above the Throne, became bewildered, and denied his mistaken thoughts of God.
rows.anchor: وفي "عرائس البقلى" قدس سره أن الله أراد ليونس معراجا ومشاهدة
